paper_metadata.title: iText2KG: Incremental Knowledge Graphs Construction Using Large Language Models
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper proposes iText2KG, a plug-and-play zero-shot method for incremental, topic-independent KG construction from unstructured documents. It uses a Document Distiller, Incremental Entity Extractor, Incremental Relation Extractor, and Graph Integrator/Visualization module to address semantic duplication and unresolved entities/relations without post-processing. The authors report superior performance against baselines for scientific-paper, website, and CV graph construction.

problem_addressed: Construct consistent knowledge graphs incrementally from raw, unstructured documents while reducing semantically duplicated or unresolved entities and relations. The objective is a topic- and document-type-independent, zero-shot alternative to ontology-dependent and supervised KG-construction pipelines.

methodology.primary_family: Zero-shot and few-shot LLM prompting (without task-specific model training)
methodology.description: Execution order: (1) Document Distiller prompts an LLM with each raw document/chunk and a user-defined JSON-like blueprint, producing and aggregating semi-filled JSON semantic blocks. (2) iEntities Matcher extracts entities from the first block, then for each later block extracts local entities and incrementally matches them to global entities by exact membership or cosine-similarity threshold, updating the global entity set. (3) iRelations Matcher receives each semantic block and either global or locally matched entities as context; it extracts relations and incrementally resolves them analogously. Global context permits direct and implied relations but can add irrelevant edges; local context targets direct relations. (4) global entities and relations are loaded into Neo4j for graph construction and visualization.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The method accepts a user-defined schema/blueprint, implemented as a predefined JSON structure parsed with LangChain, to guide which textual values are distilled. The authors explicitly distinguish this flexible blueprint from an ontology; it biases extraction toward classes/keys but is intended to remain adaptable across use cases.

evidence.excerpt: the schema is not an ontology but a blueprint... schema functions like a predefined JSON, instructing the LLM to extract particular values... for specific keys.

input_output.input_type: Raw unstructured natural-language documents: website text, scientific articles, and CVs; documents are rewritten into JSON semantic blocks before entity and relation extraction.
input_output.input_granularity: A document may be an independent document or a chunk. Processing is sequential over document-level semantic blocks; smaller chunks yield more specific semantic blocks.
input_output.output_representation: A Neo4j knowledge graph containing globally resolved entity nodes and resolved relation edges; intermediate outputs are semi-filled JSON semantic blocks and global entity/relation sets, with relation outputs evaluable as triples.

datasets: Document-Distiller evaluation set: 5 GPT-4-generated CVs, 5 company websites (text extracted), and 5 scientific articles
Annotated dataset from reference [6] for triplet consistency, augmented by manual checks for absent triplets
Threshold-estimation data: 1,500 similar entity pairs and 500 relationships generated with GPT-4 across multiple domains
Computer Science dataset and Music dataset for Table 2 triplet precision

metrics: Information Consistency categories: very different (<30%), medium (30–60%), largely consistent (60–90%), fully consistent (>90%)
Mean and standard deviation of cosine similarity for entity and relationship matching data
baselines: Graph Construction using OpenAI Function Method
LlamaIndex property-graph construction (not evaluated in entity/relation-resolution FDR tables because authors state it produces unconnected RAG-oriented subgraphs)
evaluation.setting: All experiments use GPT-4. Module 1 is assessed on three document types using schema and information consistency. Modules 2–3 are assessed for relevant-triplet precision on Computer Science and Music data under global-versus-local entity context, and for unresolved-entity/relation FDR in scientific-article-to-KG, CV-to-KG, and website-to-KG scenarios against OpenAI Function and LangChain. Ground truth combines an annotated dataset with manual checks because the authors judged the dataset non-exhaustive.

value: Experimental result: Document Distiller schema consistency was 0.97 ± 0.09 for CVs, 0.98 ± 0.04 for scientific articles, and 0.94 ± 0.13 for websites.
Experimental result: fully/largely consistent distilled content was 74.5%/25.5% for CVs, 57.1%/42.9% for scientific articles, and 56.0%/24.0% for websites; websites also had 20.0% medium consistency.
Experimental result: local entity context produced higher relevant-triplet precision than global context: Computer Science 0.94 ± 0.06 versus 0.83 ± 0.06; Music 0.90 ± 0.07 versus 0.81 ± 0.05.

Experimental result: iText2KG entity FDR was 0.01 ± 0.01 for scientific articles, 0 for CVs, and 0 for websites; relation FDR was 0.01 ± 0.01, 0, and 0, respectively. OpenAI Function/LangChain had entity FDR 0.11/0.14 (articles) and 0.31/0.29 (websites), and relation FDR 0.07/0.06 and 0.15/0.14, respectively.

value: Author claim: flexible user-defined blueprints make the method adaptable to structured and unstructured document types without a universal ontology.
Experimental result: incremental entity/relation resolution achieved lower reported FDR than the evaluated OpenAI Function and LangChain baselines for scientific-article and website scenarios.

Experimental result: separating entity extraction from relation extraction supports two operating points: local context for higher precision and global context for richer, implied-relation extraction.

Review-level inference: the explicit intermediate semantic-block and global-entity representations make the source of graph nodes and edges more inspectable than a single direct text-to-graph generation step.

value: Author-reported trade-off: global entity context enriches the graph with implied relations but lowers triplet precision by about 10 percentage points and increases the chance of irrelevant relations.
Author-reported dependency: output focus is controlled by a user-supplied blueprint whose design varies by application; there is no universal blueprint.

Review-level inference: the evaluation is limited in scale for distillation (five items of each document type), and triplet ground truth includes manual checking after the authors found the referenced dataset non-exhaustive; this limits certainty about generalization and reproducibility of those measurements.

Review-level inference: the paper reports extraction precision and unresolved-duplicate FDR, but does not report recall, end-to-end graph completeness, cost, latency, or inter-annotator agreement for manual checks.
